title: E2E experiment timeline, gating milestones, and acceptance criteria for model-v2 rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a repeatable end-to-end experiment plan, clear gating milestones, and unambiguous acceptance/rollback criteria for the staged rollout of model-v2 (a new generation of our generation kernel tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs). This ticket centralizes the timeline, statistical testing approach, instrumentation checklist, and owner matrix for the rollout so PM, Eng, SRE, and Trust teams have a single source of truth.
milestones: Discovery & hypothesis (2025-02-10 to 2025-02-14): finalize primary hypothesis: 'model-v2 will maintain baseline quality while reducing token cost by >=8% and not increasing P95 latency by >10%'. Collect offline eval sets and golden prompts.
Pre-rollout validation (2025-02-17 to 2025-02-21): offline eval on 10k prompts; perf microbench on staging GPUs; implement telemetry hooks and synthetic load harness.
Alpha internal canary (2025-02-24 to 2025-02-26): route 3% of internal traffic (logged-only) to model-v2 with no client-visible responses; validate logs and metrics.
Public A/B (5% exposure) (2025-03-01 to 2025-03-07): randomized assignment for production traffic; collect metrics for one full business week; stop early if rollback criteria hit.
Ramp (20% -> 50% -> 100%) (2025-03-08 to 2025-03-15): gradual ramp based on gate checks; final rollout and stabilization window of 7 days with post-rollout evaluation.
Post-rollout review (2025-03-22): convene cross-functional review and document lessons, update OKR progress and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Quality: Human Preference Score (HPS) shows non-inferiority: no statistically significant decrease vs. model-v1. MDE threshold: -2% with p<0.05 for two-sided test.
Latency: p95 latency change <= +10% relative to model-v1 on production traffic during the A/B window.
Errors: request error rate for model-v2 < 0.1% and no increase in 5xx rate > 0.05 percentage points.
Cost: token compute cost reduction >= 8% (measured by per-1k-token GPU-time adjusted estimate) or neutral if quality improves >3%.
Observability: all telemetry events (request_id, model_version, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, internal_latency_ms) validated in DataDog and exported to the rollout dashboard.
Safety/Trust: no increase in flagged T&S events above baseline; T&S triage confirms no new attack surface introduced.
Operational: autoscale policies respect capacity headroom; SLO alerting verifies no sustained SLO breaches during canaries.
evaluation_plan: Offline: run weighted-eval on 10k stratified prompts (control set + edge cases) using automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not used for conversational output — prefer semantic similarity and rubric-based NLU scores) and a human blind rating sample of 500 responses.

Online A/B: randomized 1:1 for primary A/B; use sequential hypothesis testing with alpha=0.05 and control for multiple comparisons on secondary metrics. Minimum detectable uplift (MDE) targeted at 2.0% for HPS with estimated sample size ~120k impressions per arm (see sample size calc in attachments).
Gold prompts & smoke tests: synthetic harness runs every deployment — must pass 100% of smoke assertions prior to any traffic ramp.
Monitoring: realtime dashboards for latency P50/P95, errors, cost per 1k tokens, HPS proxy (auto-annotated signals), drift on embedding distributions, and top-10 failing prompts by category.
Human-in-the-loop: weekly human review of 200 sampled responses during A/B to validate quality and safety signals; escalation path to Trust & Safety if pattern emerges.
statistical_plan_notes: Primary metric: Human Preference Score (HPS) aggregated weekly; treat as binomial preference test when using pairwise judgments.
Significance: two-sided alpha=0.05, use Holm-Bonferroni for up to 3 secondary hypotheses.
Stopping rule: pre-specified early stop for harm if HPS drops with p<0.01 and absolute drop >3% or if latency P95 increases beyond threshold for 10 consecutive 5-minute windows.
Sample size estimate: MDE 2%, baseline HPS 60%, power 0.8 => approx 120k impressions per arm (see calc doc).
Metrics ownership: PM owns HPS interpretation, ML Eng owns offline eval, Infra owns latency/cost instrumentation, SRE owns alert thresholds.
instrumentation_checklist: Feature flag: rollout.model_v2 (supports percentage, user bucketing, and manual kill).
Telemetry events: emit model_version, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, seq_len, inference_ms, gpu_util, trace_id for every request.
Rollout dashboard: DataDog + Looker tile with A/B aggregation, latency histograms, cost curves, and regression heatmap.
Synthetic harness: nightly job to run golden prompts and verify thresholds; results posted to CI and Slack channel #rollouts.
Alerting: PagerDuty policy for P95 latency breach, elevated error rate, and T&S incidents.
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback: any sustained P95 latency increase >25% for 10 minutes OR error rate spike >0.5% above baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
Safety rollback: any confirmed T&S pattern indicating unacceptable content generation across >20 unique prompts in a 24-hour window.
Degradation rollback: HPS decrease >3% with p<0.01 after at least 48 hours of exposure.
Operator rollback: any upstream partner reports false-positive regressions requiring rollback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: telemetry gaps cause blind spots. Mitigation: require sign-off from Infra on event parity and synthetic test pass before any traffic exposure.
Risk: inadequate sample size on niche enterprise routes. Mitigation: run targeted bucket tests for high-value customers and require opt-in canaries before ramping.
Risk: hidden regression in long-tail prompts. Mitigation: run power-law sampling and escalate to human review for top-100 long-tail failures.
Risk: cost savings degrade quality in certain domains. Mitigation: add domain-tagged evaluation and require neutral-or-better quality per domain.
deliverables: Rollout runbook (this ticket), including step-by-step ramp playbook for on-call and Eng Ops.
A/B analysis notebook and sample-size calc spreadsheet.
Instrumented dashboards + alerting tied to the rollout.feature flag.
Post-rollout cross-functional review doc and OKR update note.
